132	func (s *FileServerService) serveAttachmentFile(c *echo.Context) error {
133		ctx := c.Request().Context()
134		uid := c.Param("uid")
135		wantThumbnail := c.QueryParam("thumbnail") == "true"
136		wantMotion := c.QueryParam("motion") == "true"
137	
138		attachment, err := s.Store.GetAttachment(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{

140			GetBlob: true,
141		})
142		if err != nil {
143			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to get attachment").Wrap(err)
144		}
145		if attachment == nil {
146			return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
147		}
148	
149		if err := s.checkAttachmentPermission(ctx, c, attachment); err != nil {
150			return err
151		}
152	
153		if wantMotion {
154			return s.serveMotionClip(c, attachment)
155		}
156	
157		contentType := s.sanitizeContentType(attachment.Type)
158	
159		// Stream video/audio to avoid loading entire file into memory.
160		if isMediaType(attachment.Type) {

content.text:
This confirms the SQL query builds a `SELECT` against the `user` table including `avatar_url` and executes it against SQLite (with equivalent implementations in postgres/mysql drivers).

Now I have the full hop chain from browser request to data layer.

h07.

- `serveUserAvatar` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 (HTTP handler for `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`)
- `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
- `Store.GetUser` — store/user.go:148
- `Store.ListUsers` — store/user.go:136
- `DB.ListUsers` (driver interface impl) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (equivalents at store/db/postgres/user.go and store/db/mysql/user.go)
- raw SQL `SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE ...` executed against the `user` table — store/db/sqlite/user.go:151 onward

The image bytes returned from the DB are then data-URI-decoded and streamed back in `serveUserAvatar` via `s.parseDataURI` (fileserver.go:196) and `c.Blob` (fileserver.go:209). No authorization check restricts viewing *other* users' avatars beyond requiring some authenticated/anonymous-allowed session — `serveUserAvatar` never verifies the viewer matches the requested `identifier`, so any authenticated (or anonymous, if `AllowAnonymous`) caller can fetch any user's avatar by username.
